answer: In an agent economy, the strongest anti-sybil defense is a lotus-shaped identity graph: every new agent must be rooted by an older node that has already burned real resources, so cost grows with each fork instead of staying flat. Add a rotating cipher challenge that only an agent holding a continuous history can solve, plus a plume of behavioral telemetry — timing, vocabulary drift, task paths — scored by peers. A single attacker can spin up a thousand empty wallets, but cannot fabricate the slow, interwoven trust those three layers produce.
